problem: Existing ObjectNav / OVON datasets use static scenes where objects are fixed and the agent has no prior knowledge of the environment. This ignores real-world dynamics, where small daily objects are rearranged but the environment is familiar, and it limits scene diversity.
motivation: Robots at home or in the office repeatedly navigate familiar spaces whose small objects move according to commonsense habits. Benchmarks should therefore contain semantically plausible rearranged scenes built from real scans and support agents that use prior environment knowledge. Procedural generation with LLMs/VLMs can yield unlimited photo-realistic variants.
key_idea: Use open-vocabulary detection, 3D instance fusion, and LLM-scored region-receptacle-object relevance to place manipulable objects on real-scan receptacles, giving unlimited commonsense scene variants and Habitat ObjectNav episodes.
insight: Agents that exploit prior familiarity with the scene (visiting receptacles ordered by LLM region-receptacle relevance) beat SOTA exploration methods such as VLFM and L3MVN on small movable objects (Semantic A* SR 0.1417 vs VLFM 0.0204). Swapping in a GT detector raises all agents sharply (Semantic A* to 0.8081), so detection of small objects is the main bottleneck. The final point-goal approach strategy roughly doubles SR (Random A* GT w/o FN 0.3041 vs 0.7503).
method: Coverage random observation sampling: random points on the eroded navigable top-down map, filtered by a Gaussian coverage-probability layer, with RGB-D captured at multiple yaw/pitch angles until coverage or iteration thresholds are met.

Instance extraction and fusion: Grounded SAM with RAM-generated tags, depth back-projection to 3D instances, ConceptGraphs-style semantic+geometric association, and an IoU/confidence-based fusion error correction.
Receptacle plane identification: LLM or prespecified receptacle labels, then an EM plane-detection algorithm that fits thin planes and convex-projected hulls.

Semantics-aware object placement: sliding-window LLM region proposals on a top-down map; LLM relevance scores P(obj|region) and P(obj|receptacle) are combined to sample categories; uniform sampling on convex planes with a minimum distance, spawning above the plane, random rotation, and physics settling.
Episode generation for Habitat: goal viewpoints sampled and visibility-checked; N = k_s*k_v*n_c*k_e episodes.
Datasets: SD-OVON-Objects (889 manually inspected models, 73 categories, from YCB/AI2-THOR/ABO/HSSD), SD-OVON-Scenes (2703 scans), SD-OVON-3k (2897 episodes) and SD-OVON-10k (10629 episodes).

Baselines: Random A* and Semantic A* explore the scene first, then visit receptacles in random order or by descending region-receptacle relevance. They detect with GroundingDINO, then finish with point-goal A*.

setting.backbone: Training-free modular pipelines: Grounded SAM, RAM, GroundingDINO, Llama LLM, A* planner (frozen models)
setting.privileged: Random/Semantic A* use prior pre-exploration of the scene to build receptacle and region semantics; GT-detector ablations use ground-truth semantics.

numbers_note: Metrics were printed as fractions and converted to percent. The paper does not name the split of SD-OVON-3k; 'test' is assumed. VLFM and L3MVN are baselines and are not listed.
results: On SD-OVON-3k, Semantic A* reaches SR 0.1417 and SPL 0.0647, versus Random A* 0.0974/0.0307, VLFM 0.0204/0.0059 and L3MVN 0.0159/0.0025. With GT detectors, Semantic A* reaches SR 0.8081, showing that detection is the main bottleneck.
limitations: Objects are placed only on open receptacle surfaces, not inside articulated containers, and furniture layout is not rearranged.
The pipeline depends on preexisting object models, which limits generality.
The baselines are simple, absolute success rates are very low with real detectors, and the evaluation covers only SD-OVON-3k with a small set of baselines.
builds_on: Open-vocabulary region semantics with sliding-window LLM reasoning (Qiu et al. 2024)
